answer: A meteg appears to be printed. Host letter: very likely the ayin (the only ayin in the word, its first occurrence). Host vowel: not settled. The meteg stands between a two-dot mark (tsere-like) on its left and a qamats-shaped mark on its right, and I can't say for sure which of those belongs to the ayin and which to the following lamed.
visible_evidence: The whole word and its lower points are visible. Under the first (prefixed) lamed there is a vertical two-dot sheva, set a little lower. Under the ayin area, one row of marks reads from left to right: two horizontal dots (tsere-like), then a short separate vertical stroke, then a T-shaped qamats mark. The stroke stands alone: it is not joined to the qamats stem and has no dot under it, so it reads as a meteg and not as a vowel stem or a sheva. It sits under the body of the ayin. The left-to-right order of the marks is what makes the vowel assignment unclear, because the qamats sits to the right of (before) the stroke and the tsere-like dots to the left of (after) it. No ink from the line below reaches this row.
